moves.headline: Williams-Sonoma dropped 15% as adjusted profit fell just short and the full-year outlook was not raised
moves.summary: Comparable sales rose 5.1% and every brand grew, but adjusted EPS of $2.19 was slightly below the roughly $2.21 analysts expected, most of the margin improvement came from one-off tariff refunds, and the company only reiterated its full-year guidance.
why: Williams-Sonoma reported third-quarter results before the market opened on November 19. Net revenue grew 5.8% and comparable brand revenue 5.1%, with every brand and channel positive. Reported EPS was $2.38, up 21%, but on the adjusted basis analysts use it was $2.19, up 11.7% and a touch below the consensus of about $2.21.

The gap between the two figures is the issue. Reported gross margin rose 1.5 points to 47.6%, but 1.4 points of that came from refunds of tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Excluding the refunds, gross margin improved by only 0.1 point, with higher oil prices adding half a point of supply-chain cost. Inventories rose 7.3%, faster than sales.

The company reiterated rather than raised its full-year guidance: revenue growth of 4.7% to 7.2% and an adjusted operating margin of 17.8% to 18.2%. With nine months reported and the third-quarter adjusted margin at 17.4%, investors read the unchanged range as a sign that the holiday quarter will not bring upside.
context: Williams-Sonoma, which owns Pottery Barn and West Elm, has been one of the most profitable retailers in the home category, and its shares carried a valuation to match. When a premium-valued stock delivers a quarter that is good but not better than expected, and the improvement in profit turns out to be largely a one-off, the reaction is often larger than the numbers alone would suggest.
